messages.body:
Hi everyone,
I didn't know in which repo I should open an issue, but I just wanted to
say that I just downloaded AmberTools and this error persists on Ubuntu
20.04, even though I have no pending updates. Anyway, the conda binary
installation works great.

messages.author: Stephan Schott
messages.body:
Hi Dave,
I had this issue some time ago, so I gave it a try now to see if I can
replicate it. I also had trouble with pip, and it seems that the conda
update (line 152 of UseMiniconda.cmake) causes pip to be removed (at least
under Linux). Then, as pip is never explicitly requested, it is never
installed again, and makes pip to be missing. Now, the issue there is that
if cmake fails to update the shebang of amber.pip, it apparently also fails
to update the shebang of other python scripts. Can someone else try to
replicate this independently? I think forcing pip to be installed could be
a quick solution, but maybe someone has an idea why the conda update causes
the uninstall on the first place.
Cheers,
El jue, 14 oct 2021 a las 15:15, David A Case (<david.case.rutgers.
edu>)

messages.body:
On Thu, Oct 14, 2021, Stephan Schott wrote:
>I had this issue some time ago, so I gave it a try now to see if I can
>replicate it. I also had trouble with pip, and it seems that the conda
>update (line 152 of UseMiniconda.cmake) causes pip to be removed (at least
>under Linux). Then, as pip is never explicitly requested, it is never
>installed again, and makes pip to be missing. Now, the issue there is that
>if cmake fails to update the shebang of amber.pip, it apparently also fails
>to update the shebang of other python scripts. Can someone else try to
>replicate this independently? I think forcing pip to be installed could be
>a quick solution, but maybe someone has an idea why the conda update causes
>the uninstall on the first place.
I still can't seem to reproduce this here.  On my ubuntu 20.04 system, there
is no $AMBERHOME/miniconda/bin/pip, so the symlink to $AMBERHOME/bin is
never made, and the FixShebang script doesn't try to do anything with the
(missing) $AMBERHOME/bin/amber.pip file.  But the other amber.xxx python
scripts all seem to be correctly fixed.
The behavior in the paragraph above is what the code looks like it should be
doing, and what was intended.  One thing to try would be to uncomment line
36 in cmake/FixCondaShebang/FixCondaShebang.cmake.  This will indicate what
order all these fixes are done in, which might somehow not be be that same
on all machines.  Or, if amber.pip is present in the list, try to figure
out why that is.  One could also add a check on the existence of ${FILE}
inside the loop starting at line 42, so that configuretime_file_replace()
won't try to work on a non-existent file, and hence won't fail.
Since you are able to get things to fail, you might be able to track down the
problem.
But my further question is this: does any workflow really make use of
$AMBERHOME/bin/{amber.conda,amber.ipython,amber.jupyter}?  I have a feeling
that the answer might be "no", and we could just skip this whole process
entirely.
...thanks...dac

messages.author: Stephan Schott
messages.body:
Hi again,
.David I had a mishap with the updater within cmake. It was not running the
updater properly (maybe some permission issues?), but after running the
python updater by hand, everything seems to be working on my side :D, sorry
for the confusion.
.German please make sure to start from a clean build directory, and with a
fully updated amber source tree. You can execute ./update_amber --update in
the root dir and make sure you get the patch up until update.10. It should
do the trick.
Cheers,
El jue, 14 oct 2021 a las 17:44, David A Case (<david.case.rutgers.
edu>)

messages.body:
*Try one more thing:** ls -l /home/pbarletta/amber20//bin/amber.pip:*
/home/pbarletta/amber20//bin/amber.pip ->
/home/pbarletta/amber20/miniconda/bin/pip
in red, and when I go to /home/pbarletta/amber20/miniconda/bin, there's no
*pip* executable there.
The *FixCondaShebang/FixCondaShebang.cmake* error shows up at line 26, so
the following lines are never reached.
The broken symlink is created on lines 116-118 of *cmake_install.cmake*. If
I comment out those lines, the installation seems to work fine and even
python tools like *pdb4amber* seem to work, although of course I have no
idea what I'm doing.
Let me know if there's anything else I can do to help.
Cheers!

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Thu, Oct 14, 2021, German P. Barletta wrote:
>The broken symlink is created on lines 116-118 of *cmake_install.cmake*. If
>I comment out those lines, the installation seems to work fine and even
>python tools like *pdb4amber* seem to work, although of course I have no
>idea what I'm doing.
I can't seem to find any file called cmake_install.cmake.  The place I see
that creates that symlink is at lines 253-256 of
amber20_src/cmake/UseMiniconda.cmake.  There is it protected by a check to
make sure that the miniconda/bin/pip file actually exists.
The fact that I don't have the same files as you have probably explains why
we are not getting the same results.  Can you say what folder this file is
in? Are you sure you have freshly extracted AmberTools21.tar.bz2 in a clean
folder?
(I may be missing something obvious, but I don't see what it is right now.)
...thx...dac

messages.author: German P. Barletta
messages.body:
Definitely working on a clean folder with the latest AmberTools. Though I
did find this:
The file it's amber20_src/build/cmake_install.cmake and it's created by the
*run_cmake* script. If I backup that file:
mv cmake_install.cmake backup_cmake_install.cmake
and run the *run_cmake* script again (so the *build* folder is not clean),
I get a new cmake_install.cmake, different from the previous one in those
exact 116-118 lines:
if("x${CMAKE_INSTALL_COMPONENT}x" STREQUAL "xPythonx" OR NOT
CMAKE_INSTALL_COMPONENT)
execute_process(COMMAND /usr/bin/cmake -E create_symlink
$ENV{DESTDIR}${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/miniconda/bin/pip
$ENV{DESTDIR}${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/bin/amber.pip)
endif()
If I start all over again, moving AmberTools21.tar.bz2 to a new clean
folder, and running the *run_cmake* script inside the *build* folder, then
I get the same old cmake_install.cmake script, with the same 116-118 lines,
creating that symlink.
Could it be, then, that you're not starting from a fresh folder? :P
Here're the cmake scripts. I'm pasting them in plain text since I don't
know if this list supports gmails link embedding:
old backed up cmake_install.cmake:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/tpxn4c1ulccjetr/backup_cmake_install.cmake?dl=0
new cmake_install.cmake:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/7lb6uzzb0q4vnlp/cmake_install.cmake?dl=0

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Oct 15, 2021, German P. Barletta wrote:
>
>Could it be, then, that you're not starting from a fresh folder? :P
I think your analysis is correct, but I'm still not sure of the correct fix.
It may have something to do with trying to update cmake components, since
the update happens *during* the cmake run (i.e. it is initialized by cmake).
I won't be able to work on this for a couple of weeks, but others are
welcome to try.  We either need to make creationg of symlink itself safe
when the target doesn't exist, or just remove creating these symlinks
altogether.
....dac
